newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk to transfer 10 pct of shares to staff.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk to transfer 10 pct of shares to staff.

text.p: An agreement to transfer a 10 percent stake in RAO Norilsky Nikel, one of the world's biggest metals producers, to its employees is ready but not signed, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
Sergei Vetchinin told Reuters that agreement would be signed in one or two days and the delay was due to the illness of a State Property Committee official who dealt with the matter.
The 10 percent stake will form Norilsk's employee share fund (FARP in Russian), allocated to employees during voucher privatisation in 1992-93.
Traders said the transfer of shares to Norilsk Nickel employees would have a negative impact on the share price as some of the shares would inevitably land on the secondary market.
At 1415 GMT Norilsk Nickel was traded at $6.23 after $6.16 at Wednesday's close.
Previously Vetchinin had said that Norilsk authorities did not want the shares to be sold immediately, but did not say how management would prevent staff from selling their shares.

Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) won a 38 percent stake in Norilsk Nickel under a loans-for-shares scheme, in which the government gave stakes in Russia's biggest companies as collateral for loans to banks.
Foreign investors, including CS First Boston with a six percent stake, have about 12 percent of the company's shares.
Norilsk management has five percent of shares.
